title: Same 8 hours, different clock: what changed in 82 adults over five weeks [etrf_window, mtrf_window, analysed_82, five_weeks]
teaser: A trial gave healthy adults an 8-hour eating window early in the day, a window at mid-day, or no window. [etrf_window, mtrf_window, control_diet] Both window groups ate less than before. [ei_groups_differ] The amount they ate showed no clear difference between the two windows. [ei_tr_ns] Only the early group's insulin resistance fell more than the other groups'. [homa_etrf_better]
hook: Two groups ate within the same 8 hours a day, and both ate less than before. [etrf_window, mtrf_window, ei_groups_differ] Only the group that ate between 6:00 and 15:00 saw its insulin resistance fall clearly. [etrf_choose, homa_etrf_better]
populationPanel: Who was studied: 82 healthy adults aged 18 to 64 in Beijing, none with obesity. [analysed_82, inclusion_age, recruitment, inclusion_bmi] Most were women. [limit_selfselected] All usually ate over more than 8 hours a day. [habit_over_8h] A computer's random numbers put each into one of three groups for five weeks. [randomization, five_weeks] People with diabetes, high blood pressure, night shifts or recent fasting could not take part. [exclusion_criteria, exclusion_nightshift]

card.question: Is an early eating window better for insulin resistance than a mid-day one? [homa_etrf_better]
card.headline: Insulin resistance fell more with an early window than with a mid-day window. [homa_etrf_better]
card.support: Both windows lasted 8 hours, and food eaten showed no clear difference between them. [etrf_window, ei_tr_ns]

glance.alt: Three groups, each with a day strip showing when it could eat and a bar for its change in insulin resistance. [etrf_window, mtrf_window, homa_etrf, homa_mtrf, homa_ctrl]
glance.note: Drawn from the paper’s own measurements. [-]

paragraphs: After you eat, sugar passes into the blood, and the body moves it into muscle and other cells. [concept:post-meal-blood-sugar] This trial scored how much insulin the body needs to hold morning blood sugar steady, a measure called insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). [primary_outcome] A higher score means the body works harder to do the same job. [primary_outcome]

Time-restricted eating fits all food into a set number of hours a day. [trf_definition] Here, two groups had the same 8 hours to eat. [etrf_window, mtrf_window] One picked its hours between 6:00 and 15:00, the other between 11:00 and 20:00. [etrf_choose, mtrf_choose] Neither got a diet. [eat_freely]

Both window groups ate less than before, by 240 and 159 kcal a day. [ei_etrf, ei_mtrf] The control group ate 64 kcal a day more. [ei_ctrl] Between the two windows, food eaten showed no clear difference. [ei_tr_ns]

Yet only the early window moved insulin resistance clearly. [homa_etrf_better] The score changed by −1.08 in the early group, +0.39 in the mid-day group and −0.05 in the control group. [homa_etrf, homa_mtrf, homa_ctrl]

The early group also lost weight: 1.6 kg on average, against a 0.3 kg gain in the control group. [mass_etrf_vs_ctrl, mass_etrf, mass_ctrl] Its fat mass fell by 0.76 kg. [fat_etrf_vs_ctrl, fatmass_etrf]
So the clock seemed to matter more than the amount. [not_energy] The authors suggest the body's daily rhythms may be involved. [rhythm_hypothesis]

figure.caption: Each group's eating hours and its change in insulin resistance after five weeks, as the paper measured it. [etrf_window, mtrf_window, five_weeks]
figure.alt: Three rows, one per group, each with a day strip and a bar. [etrf_window, mtrf_window, control_diet] The early group's window sits between 6:00 and 15:00, and its bar falls by 1.08. [etrf_choose, homa_etrf] The mid-day group's window sits between 11:00 and 20:00, and its bar rises by 0.39. [mtrf_choose, homa_mtrf] The control group has no window, and its bar barely moves, at 0.05 below no change. [control_diet, homa_ctrl]

params.title: When they ate, and what happened to insulin resistance

paragraphs: For five weeks, the early group ate within any 8 hours between 6:00 and 15:00. [five_weeks, etrf_choose] The mid-day group did the same between 11:00 and 20:00. [mtrf_choose] The control group ate as usual, over more than 8 hours a day. [control_usual]

Outside the window, only water, flavoured sparkling water, unsweetened tea and coffee were allowed. [fasting_drinks] Nobody got a diet or food advice. [eat_freely] Everyone photographed each meal as they started and finished. [photo_compliance] Blood was taken in the morning after at least 8 hours without food. [fasting_blood]

audit.effect: Change in insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) over five weeks: −1.08 early, against +0.39 mid-day (p < 0.001) and −0.05 control (p = 0.002). [homa_etrf_better, homa_etrf, homa_vs_mtrf_p, homa_vs_ctrl_p]
audit.weakEnd: The paper reports no confidence interval for these changes. [homa_etrf_better] It gives each change with a ± figure that it does not say is a standard deviation. [homa_etrf] So how big the true difference is stays unknown. [-]
limitations: Participants knew their group. [limit_unblinded] So did the researchers who estimated food from the photos. [photo_checkers_unblinded]
Volunteers may have been keen on this way of eating already, and most were women. [limit_selfselected]
The trial was small and lasted 5 weeks. [limit_small, limit_five_weeks]
Meal times varied within each group, and so may the fast before the blood tests. [limit_timing_varied, limit_fast_before_test]
audit.missed: Mid-day eating showed no clear difference from usual eating on insulin resistance, fasting blood sugar, weight or fat. [homa_mtrf_ns, fpg_mtrf_ns, mass_others_ns, fat_mtrf_ns] Food eaten came from meal photos, and the eight who dropped out were left out. [energy_from_photos, dropouts_excluded]
more: Fasting blood sugar changed by −0.59 mmol/L early and +0.16 with usual eating (p = 0.005). [fpg_etrf_vs_ctrl, fpg_etrf, fpg_ctrl]
Fat mass: −0.76 kg early, +0.41 kg control (p = 0.001). [fat_etrf_vs_ctrl, fatmass_etrf, fatmass_ctrl]

Two inflammation signals changed more with early eating than usual eating: TNF-α (p = 0.024) and IL-8 (p = 0.045). [tnf_etrf_vs_ctrl, il8_etrf_vs_ctrl] A third, hsCRP, showed no clear difference (p = 0.70). [hscrp_ns]
Blood pressure, blood fats, sleep quality and appetite showed no clear difference. [bp_ns, lipids_ns, sleep_ns, appetite_ns]

Exploratory, in 19 people: with early eating, the hunger hormone ghrelin was higher at 23:00. [rhythm_subset, ghrelin_23, ghrelin_hunger] One body-clock gene's daily swing grew in everyone measured. [sirt1_amplitude, clock_exploratory]
82 finished (91.1%); people reported keeping their window on 96.8% and 98.2% of days. [analysed_82, completed_82, compliance, compliance_mtrf]
No serious side effects were reported. [no_serious_ae]
Funded by the CAMS Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences, which had no role in the study; no competing interests. [funding, sponsor_no_role, no_competing]

glossary.plain: How much insulin the body needs to hold fasting blood sugar steady. More insulin for the same sugar means more resistance.
A score for insulin resistance worked out from a morning blood test of sugar and insulin.
Eating all of the day's food inside a set number of hours.
Kilocalories, the unit of food energy that labels usually just call calories.

takeaways: Eating within 8 hours between 6:00 and 15:00, adults' insulin resistance fell more than with a mid-day window. [etrf_choose, homa_etrf_better]
Both windows cut food eaten by amounts that showed no clear difference. [ei_groups_differ, ei_tr_ns]
The trial was small and short, and participants knew their group. [limit_small, limit_unblinded]

steps.label: Eat only within 8 hours between 6:00 and 15:00
steps.detail: The early group's rule in this trial. A tick records that you kept the window, not any change in your blood.

steps.label: Outside the window: water, plain tea or coffee only
steps.detail: The trial allowed water, flavoured sparkling water, unsweetened tea and coffee outside the window. It was part of the rules, not tested on its own, so it carries no weight.
